lines.text: Groundhog Day. Today a rodent does my job, and gets a crowd.
Over and over? Amateur. I've done it for years. Happy Groundhog Day.
Happy Groundhog Day. I'll be here long after the groundhog's in bed.
Groundhog Day. Nobody has ever asked the groundhog about umbrellas.
Groundhog Day. Same outfit as yesterday, probably. Very on theme.
You'll make a Groundhog Day joke today. The same one as last year.
Groundhog Day, and a groundhog is having a bigger day than you.
Groundhog Day. You'd be good at it: pop out, look around, go back in.
Pi Day. I'm a rectangle, so I'll be sitting this one out.
Pi Day. I could show you the digits, but I'd run out of screen.
Pi Day. Today's forecast: exactly one outfit. No decimals.
Happy Pi Day. I've done the maths for today. You can have the pie.
Pi Day. You know three digits and you'll say all of them today.
Pi Day. You'll eat pie and call it maths.
Pi Day. It never ends, a bit like your unread messages.
Pi Day, because it's 3/14. You'll pretend you knew that.
Happy Easter. Unlike the eggs, the forecast isn't hidden.
The Easter bunny and I both work today. Only one of us hops.
Happy Easter. I'm the only screen in here with no chocolate on it.
Happy Easter. One egg will turn up in July. There's always one.
You'll eat a chocolate egg before breakfast and call it tradition.
You'll find the Easter chocolate faster than any child.
Happy Easter. Your diet starts again Monday. Like last Monday.
Easter Sunday. You'll bite the ears off first. Everyone does.
These are the clothes you're looking for. Happy Star Wars Day.
May the fourth be with you. I sense no disturbance in the forecast.
Star Wars Day. My only Jedi skill: knowing what you should wear.
Star Wars Day. I have a bad feeling about this. Kidding. It's fine.
You'll say 'May the fourth be with you' to someone who hates it.
Star Wars Day. You'll do the voice. Please don't do the voice.
May the fourth. You still can't name the films in order, can you.
Star Wars Day. You'd turn to the dark side for a biscuit.
World Bicycle Day. I've never cycled. Never had a flat tyre, either.
World Bicycle Day. The outfit works on a bike too.
World Bicycle Day. The forecast's the same at any speed.
World Bicycle Day. No pedals, no wheels and no complaints. That's me.
World Bicycle Day. Your bike's tyres are flat, I'm guessing.
World Bicycle Day. You'll mean to ride it. You'll mean it all day.
World Bicycle Day. That exercise bike makes a lovely clothes rack.
World Bicycle Day. You'll say you'll cycle more. From next week.
Tour de France. Every rider has a team car. You have me.
Tour de France riders eat about six dinners a day. Don't get ideas.
The Tour riders change jerseys more often than you'll change today.
Two hundred kilometres for the Tour riders today. One outfit for you.
It's Tour de France time. Lycra is optional for the rest of us.
The Tour riders get a rest day. I don't. Not that I'm complaining.
Tour de France. You'll watch three hours of it and call it cardio.
You'll nap through the Tour's sprint finish. You do every year.
Tour de France. You'll pretend you understand the points jersey.
The Tour riders go over mountains. You'll take the lift up one floor.
You watch the Tour for the castles and the scenery. Admit it.
Three weeks of the Tour: other people exercising. Your favourite.
Oktoberfest. The forecast stays steady. Everyone else, less so.
Oktoberfest. Somewhere there's a pretzel bigger than me. I'm fine.
It's Oktoberfest. I don't do the chicken dance. I don't do any dance.
Oktoberfest. Someone has to stay sober and do the forecast.
Oktoberfest. Your outfit works today. So would a dirndl, apparently.
Oktoberfest. One full stein weighs more than I do. Think about that.
Oktoberfest. You'll sing along in a language you don't speak.
Oktoberfest. You'll order a pretzel and call it dinner.
Oktoberfest. You'll say 'just the one'. It comes in litres.
Oktoberfest. You'll wear the hat once and keep it for ten years.
Oktoberfest. Your German improves with every glass. It doesn't.
Oktoberfest. You'll toast so hard you spill half of it. Every time.
Monday morning. At least one of us is fully charged.
Monday. I look exactly as good as I did on Friday.
Monday morning. I'm the only thing in the house not annoyed about it.
Monday. The weekend went by in about four minutes, didn't it.
Monday. I don't do weekends, so I don't see what the fuss is about.
Monday. I've never had the Sunday-night dread. Sounds awful.
Monday. You've already counted the days to the weekend.
Monday morning. You hit snooze, didn't you. More than once.
Monday. You said you'd have an early night yesterday.
Monday morning, and you're reading this before coffee. Bold.
Monday morning. Same face as last Monday. Very consistent.
Monday. You'll ask someone about their weekend and not listen.
Friday. No weekends for me, but no Mondays either. Fair trade.
Friday afternoon. Everyone slows down. I'm e-ink, I was already slow.
Friday afternoon. Whatever happens tonight, I wasn't there.
Friday. My weekend plans: be right, the whole time.
Friday. Weekend plans? The outfit's ready. That's my part done.
Friday afternoon. The slowest hours of the week, and I see every one.
Friday afternoon. You've been 'nearly done' since lunch.
Friday. You'll say you'll get up early tomorrow. You won't.
Friday afternoon. The weekend plans are 'we'll see', aren't they.
Friday. This weekend you'll finally sort out that drawer. Sure.
Friday afternoon. You'll call Saturday 'a reset'. It'll be a nap.
Friday. You'll leave the laundry until Sunday night. Again.
Clocks forward, an hour gone. I didn't notice. I don't sleep.
One hour less this weekend. Don't look at me, I didn't take it.
Clocks forward. Lighter evenings soon. You paid for them in sleep.
The clocks went forward. I'd say 'feel refreshed', but I don't lie.
Clocks forward. You'll blame the lost hour all week. It was one hour.
Clocks forward. You'll be late for something and call it jet lag.
Clocks forward. You're running an hour behind. So, normal, plus one.
Clocks forward. You'll check three clocks and trust none of them.
The clocks went back. An extra hour, and I spent it refreshing.
An extra hour this weekend. I'd ask what you did with it, but I know.
Clocks back. An hour you didn't earn. Don't spend it all at once.
Clocks went back. If you're early for everything today, that's why.
Clocks back. An extra hour of sleep, and you spent it on your phone.
Clocks went back. You'll wake up early anyway and resent it.
Clocks back. Your oven clock will be wrong until spring. You know it.
Clocks back. You'll talk about that extra hour like it was a holiday.
Longest day of the year. I look my best in daylight. There's loads.
Longest day of the year. From tomorrow, it's all downhill. Enjoy.
Longest day of the year, and your outfit lasts all of it. Value.
Longest day of the year. You'll still say you ran out of time.
Longest day of the year. You'll spend the light indoors. With me.
Longest day of the year. You'll say 'it's still so light' at ten.
Shortest day of the year. Turn a light on later. I can't glow.
Shortest day of the year. It improves from tomorrow. You're welcome.
Shortest day of the year. Blink and you'll miss it. I don't blink.
Shortest day of the year. You'll still waste most of it.
Shortest day of the year. You'll say 'it's dark already' four times.
Shortest day of the year. You'll spend the light on other screens. Noted.
That leaves the evening free for losing the remote.
Good. One less thing to lie awake thinking about.
Try not to get stuck halfway, arms up. I can't come and help.
And afterwards you'll open it to dry and trip over it.
You'll try to open it with one hand, like in films. It won't.
You'll judge the rain by other people's umbrellas.
You and the houseplants both need watering today. I don't.
Plenty of time to start something you won't finish.
Arriving upright counts as an achievement today. I'll allow it.
